title: Degenerates is playing Off-Broadway at Playwright’s Horizon now throu...
transcript: This play about incels has become one of the hottest tickets off Broadway. and having now seen it, it's pretty easy to see why. It comes to us from theater power couple, playwright else went and director Emma Rose went, the team behind last season's five hour epic, initiative. I remember leaving that show feeling like I could watch five hours more of that, and I honestly felt very similarly coming out of this show. The writing is so engaging and you become invested in these characters so quickly that by the time it ends, you wanna keep up with these characters, you wanna see what's gonna happen to them next. And that's certainly an unexpected thing to say about a play about incels. It really gets you to understand and sympathize with these characters, who, yes, have their issues, and the play makes no excuses for them. but it also gives them dignity and allows them to be seen as humans and not just as punchlines. It asks the question, how did these guys end up like this? And is there still hope for them? I'm not gonna lie, this play can be uncomfortable to watch at times. whether that is the language that the characters use, the situations that they find themselves in, or some of the topics that are discussed, which can be quite heavy. I mean, this play literally opens up with someone on a suicide hotline. But I also think it is this play’s unflinchingness and unwillingness to shy away from some of these darker topics that really makes it so special. It's been talked about as a potential Pulitzer Prize finalist, and I could definitely see that in its future. But even if not, Degenerates is definitely going to be a Broadway Ben must see. It is basically sold out, but if you can get a ticket, go. Because I don't know if this play could ever be on Broadway, so I definitely wouldn't bank on a transfer, and the safest option is just going to be to see it during its current run.
reasoning: Strong rave with Pulitzer prediction, 'must see' label, and urgent recommendation to catch the current run since a transfer is unlikely.
